graphs-topo_sort_dag.desc: Understand topological sorting and directed acyclic graphs, and their constraints.

graphs_adv-proofs.desc: Be able to walk through and understand some advanced graph proofs and algorithmic graph reductions.

internet.desc: Packets, TCP and UDP, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, prefixes, NAT, ports, routing as shortest paths (link-state and distance-vector), latency and the speed of light, DNS, and network layers.

html.desc: Understand HTML language, its typical usage, and how to work with a basic HTML document

web_apis.desc: The main topic of the Web APIs chapter.

http.desc: Understand how HTTP requests work and their purpose.

json.desc: The JSON data format: objects, arrays, and key-value pairs.

xml.desc: The XML data format, compared with JSON.

api.desc: Understand what an API is, CRUD operations, how to create an API.

curl.desc: Understand how to use curl in the command line for testing APIs.

css_js.desc: CSS rules, selectors, the cascade, the box model, flexbox and responsive layout; JavaScript for Python programmers, the DOM, event listeners, data attributes, fetch with async/await, and serving a site with Express.

digital_logic.desc: Transistors as switches, CMOS inverters and NAND gates, logic gates and truth tables, NAND universality, half and full adders, ripple-carry addition, and subtraction with two's complement.

long lat.desc: Define longitude and latitude as measures of geographic coordinate system

haversine.desc: Understand and use the haversine formula to find the distance between two points on a sphere

geocoding.desc: Understand the process of geocoding and reverse geocoding.

plotly.desc: Use python to make a geographical world map and add locations of longitude and latitude on it.

discrete_probability_counting.desc: The main topic of the Discrete Probability and Random Variables chapter.

probability_independent.desc: Understand how to find probability of independent events. Understand that all probabilities must sum to 1.

probability_dependent.desc: Understand the basis of conditional probability and how to find the probability of two dependent events .

correlation_causation.desc: Understand the concept of "correlation does not imply causation".

uniform_distribution.desc: Understand the concept of uniform distribution. Recall bell curve from previous chapters.

random_variables.desc: Discrete random variables, probability mass functions, expected value, variance, and linearity of expectation.

combinatorics.desc: Understand how to complete combinatorics problems. Understand the binomial distribution.

factorial.desc: Understand how the factorial operation works.

binomial_series.desc: Understand how we can use the binomial theorem for negative integers and for fractions.

permutations.desc: Understand the process of permutations, how to find them and how to apply them to sorting problems.

binomial_distribution.desc: The binomial distribution: BINS conditions, formula, mean and standard deviation, the 10% condition.

geometric_distribution.desc: The geometric distribution: formula, mean and standard deviation, memorylessness.

exponential_distribution.desc: The exponential distribution for waiting times.

conditional_prob.desc: The main topic of the Conditional Probability chapter.

probability_conditional.desc: Understand how to calculate conditional probability. Be able to use the chain rule for probability

bayes.desc: Understand Bayes' theorem and be able to apply it to new information

monty-hall-prob.desc: Understand the monty hall problem and the application of Bayes' theorem behind it.

intro_markov.desc: Understand the basics of Markov Chains in statistics. Be able to use properties of Markov chains, draw Markov Chains and understand the basics of Hidden Markov Models and emissions.

transition_matrices.desc: Understand how to represent Markov Chains with transition matrices. Be able to use linear algebra on these matrices to find next and future states. Understand how to find steady state distributions

antiderivatives.desc: Understand how to find general antiderivatives, inverse derivative rules, and find general solutions and specific solutions. Find indefinite integrals

riemann_sums.desc: The main topic of the Riemann Sums and Sigma Notation chapter.

riemann.desc: Understand how to calculate riemann sums and area under the curve.

trap_rule.desc: Understand how to utilize the trapezoidal rule as a method of calculating areas under curves.

definite_integral.desc: Understand how to calculate definite integrals and their properties.

ftc_avg_val.desc: Understand and apply both parts of the FTC, and be able to evaluate definite integrals. Also, understand how to find the average value of a function.

arc_length.desc: Use integration to calculate the length of a curve or arc. Understand how to integrate for both 2D and 3D functions.

continuous_distributions.desc: The main topic of the Continuous Distributions chapter.

cdf_pdf.desc: Understand how to interpret continuous uniform distributions, cumulative probability functions, and probability density functions.

normal_distribution.desc: Understand how to find the PDF of a normal distribution, and why it is important.

sampling_distributions.desc: Sampling distributions of the sample mean and sample proportion.

bootstrap.desc: Bootstrap standard errors and percentile intervals.

permutation_test.desc: Permutation tests and p-values by shuffling.

confidence_intervals.desc: Estimating a population proportion with a confidence interval

hypothesis_testing_logic.desc: Understanding the logic behind a significance test

p_values.desc: Interpreting p-values and deciding whether to reject the null hypothesis

type_i_ii_errors.desc: Avoiding Type I and Type II errors, and understanding the power of a test

critical_values.desc: One-tailed, two-tailed tests, and critical values

t_distribution.desc: Be able to describe the properties of the t-distribution, determine degrees of freedom, verify conditions for inference about a mean, and recognize matched-pairs data.

mean_confidence_intervals.desc: Be able to construct and interpret a confidence interval for a population mean, including the mean of matched-pairs differences.

significance_tests.desc: Be able to conduct and interpret a significance test for a population mean, including matched-pairs differences.

difference_of_means.desc: Be able to construct a confidence interval and conduct a significance test for the difference between two independent population means.

two_sample_proportions.desc: Confidence intervals and significance tests for the difference between two population proportions.

regression_slope_basics.desc: The main topic of the Regression Basics for the Slope chapter.

slope_conditions.desc: Be able to verify the conditions (linear relationship, constant standard deviation, independence, normality of residuals) required for inference about the slope of a regression model.

slope_interval.desc: Be able to construct and interpret a confidence interval for the slope of a regression model, including margin of error, standard error, and the effect of sample size on interval width.

slope_test.desc: Be able to identify hypotheses, calculate the t test statistic and p-value, and justify a claim for a significance test about the slope of a regression model.

regression_output.desc: Be able to identify the slope, y-intercept, r-squared, standard deviation of residuals, and standard error of the slope from computer regression output (minitab), and describe the association

inference_selection.desc: Be able to select and justify the appropriate inference procedure (confidence interval or significance test) for a scenario involving the slope of a regression model.

lin_reg_r2_anova.desc: The main topic of the Evaluating the Fit of a Linear Regression Model chapter.

adjusted_r_squared.desc: Sums of squares, R-squared as explained variation, and adjusted R-squared.

regression_anova.desc: The ANOVA table and F-test for regression.

chi_square_statistic.desc: Compute the chi-square statistic from observed and expected counts and find critical values from a chi-square table.

chi_square_goodness_of_fit.desc: Interpret a chi-square goodness-of-fit test for a single categorical variable.

chi_square_independence.desc: Interpret a chi-square test for independence using a contingency table.

chi_square_homogeneity.desc: Interpret a chi-square test for homogeneity and distinguish it from a test for independence.

gas-temp.desc: How the temperature of a gas relates to the speed of the molecules

abs-zero.desc: Be able to define Absolute zero and the Kelvin temperature scale

ideal-gas-law.desc: Understand the Ideal Gas Law, Boyle's law, and Charles Law.

temp kinetic.desc: Understand molar heat capacity, adiabatic compression and decompression, and calculate temperature change.

energy_heat_trans.desc: Understand how much energy is used in a heat transfer, and what factors it depends on

engine.desc: Understand how piston engines work, how they generate fuel and their side effects, and how to use engine terminology.

second_law.desc: Microstates and macrostates, entropy (S = k ln W and Q/T), the second law, the Carnot limit on engine efficiency, and the limits on refrigerators and heat pumps.

u-substitution.desc: The main topic of the u-Substitution chapter.

usub.desc: Understand how to integrate functions using u-sub.

polar_calc_derivative.desc: Understand how to find slopes of polar functions.

polar_calc_integrals.desc: Understand how to find areas of general polar functions.

diff_eqs.desc: Be able to solve ordinary differential equations, logistic DE's, and separable differential equations.

slope_fields.desc: Be able to work with slope fields, both graphing and identifying.

euler_method.desc: Be able to apply euler's method to approximate differential equations.

sequences2.desc: Evaluate limits of sequences and determine whether sequences converge or diverge.

monotonic_bounded_sequences.desc: Determine whether a sequence is monotonic or bounded, and use those properties to reason about convergence.

sequence_applications.desc: Use recursive and explicit sequences to model applications such as compound interest and population growth.

series_calc.desc: Understand how to use sequences to form series. Determine convergence and divergence of series.

series_tests.desc: Understand how to apply the series tests, including TFD, Integral Test, Ratio Test, both Comparison Tests, and the Root Test.

power_series.desc: Be able to use calculate the radius and intervals of convergence. Use calculus to approximate power series integrals and derivatives.

taylor_series.desc: The main topic of the Taylor and Maclaurin Series chapter.

euler_formula.desc: Euler's formula, the complex exponential, and polar form of complex numbers.

fourier_series.desc: Fourier series, harmonics, spectra and the FFT, sampling, filters, and speaker crossovers.

pop_prop.desc: Understand how the binomial distribution models sample outcomes when the true population is known. Be able to use the beta distribution.

change_var.desc: Understand how changing variables effects a PDF and CDF

volume_double_integral.desc: Be able to find volumes of regions using double integrals using iterated integration. Understand fubini's theorem.

double_int_regions.desc: Be able to evaluate integrals over non-rectangular regions.

double_int_mass_center.desc: The main topic of the Mass, Charge, and Center of Mass chapter.

double_int_applications.desc: Be able to use double integrals to apply to real life problems including lamina densities, total mass, center of mass, and surface area.

multiv_distributions.desc: Be able to create probability distributions for functions relying on multiple variables.

multiv_normal.desc: Understand how to process different multi-variable normal distribution.

numerical_double_int.desc: Be able to use integration (and double integration) to approximate probability density functions.

classification_regression.desc: The main topic of the Classification and Regression chapter.

palmer_penguins.desc: The Palmer Penguins dataset used throughout the machine-learning unit.

rmse_mae_accuracy.desc: RMSE, MAE, and accuracy; baseline models.

train_val_test.desc: The main topic of the The Training, Validation, and Testing Process chapter.

overfitting.desc: Overfitting and underfitting; training versus validation error.

cross_validation.desc: k-fold cross-validation and the one-standard-error rule.

standardization.desc: The main topic of the Standardizing Data chapter.

one_hot_encoding.desc: One-hot encoding, the dummy variable trap, and ordinal categories.

feature_scaling.desc: Standardization and min-max scaling, and which methods need them.

least_squares.desc: The main topic of the Least Squares chapter.

simple_linear.desc: Simple linear regression: predictor, response, slope, intercept, and interpretation.

multiple_regression.desc: Multiple regression with a design matrix, solved by least squares.

simpsons_paradox.desc: Simpson's paradox: a trend that reverses within groups.

lin_reg_gradient_descent.desc: The main topic of the Linear Regression and Gradient Descent chapter.

learning_rate.desc: The learning rate and why it must not be too large or too small.

minibatch_sgd.desc: Mini-batch and stochastic gradient descent, and epochs.

logistic_regr.desc: The main topic of the Logistic Regression chapter.

sigmoid_log_odds.desc: The sigmoid function, odds, log odds, and odds ratios.

log_loss.desc: Log loss (cross-entropy) and maximum likelihood for binary classification.

confusion.desc: The main topic of the Evaluating Classification Systems chapter.

roc_auc.desc: ROC curves, precision-recall curves, and AUC.

knn_classifier.desc: The k-nearest neighbor classifier and regressor.

curse_of_dimensionality.desc: Why nearest neighbors break down with many features.

stemming_lemmatization.desc: Understand the processes of stemming and lemmatization.

bag_of_words.desc: Tokenizing, stop words, and bag-of-words count matrices.

bayes_classifier.desc: Understand how to use multivariate and Gaussian distributions to create bayes classifiers.

naive_bayes.desc: Naive Bayes classifiers, Laplace smoothing, and log probabilities.

gaussian_bayes.desc: Gaussian and multivariate Gaussian class-conditional models.

explaining_away.desc: Explaining away and inference by enumeration in Bayesian networks.

decision_trees_classification.desc: The main topic of the Decision Trees for Classification chapter.

decision_trees.desc: Decision trees, Gini impurity, entropy, and information gain.

bagging_random_forest.desc: The main topic of the Bagging and Random Forests chapter.

random_forest.desc: Random forests, out-of-bag error, and feature importance.

boosting.desc: Boosting: AdaBoost and gradient boosting with weak learners.

adaboost.desc: The AdaBoost algorithm and its weight updates.

glm.desc: Generalized linear models: random component, linear predictor, and link function.

poisson_regression.desc: Poisson regression fit by Newton's method (IRLS).

k_means.desc: The k-means clustering algorithm, k-means++, and the elbow method.

nn_regression.desc: The main topic of the Neural Networks for Regression chapter.

neural_networks.desc: Neurons, layers, activation functions, and training neural networks.

pytorch_basics.desc: PyTorch tensors, automatic differentiation, nn.Sequential, and optimizers.

early_stopping.desc: Early stopping with a validation set.

softmax.desc: The softmax function and multi-class cross-entropy loss.

deep_learning.desc: The main topic of the Deep Learning chapter.

backpropagation.desc: Backpropagation and the chain rule in neural networks.

z_table.desc: Be able to use the standard normal table to find an area from a z-score and a z-score from an area.

t_table.desc: Be able to find a t* critical value from degrees of freedom and confidence level, and bound a P-value with the t table.

chi_square_table.desc: Be able to find a chi-square critical value and bound a P-value with the chi-square table.

critical_value_tables.desc: Be able to connect a confidence level or tail area to the critical value that cuts it off.
